title: Qualify on boundary cases and twins
statement: Qualify anyone whose labels will set a standard on boundary cases and their opposite-value twins, not only clear cases, since clear-case accuracy can hide shared boundary failures.
example: Two candidates scored 9/10 on clear positives and nearest neighbours but 3/10 and 2/10 on boundary cases and 3/10 each on opposite-value cases.
detail: A blind, synthetic 60-item qualification round tested whether two candidates could reproduce a frozen scheme for coding teaching principles into typed fields. Both scored 9/10 on positives and nearest neighbours and 10/10 on missingness and scope gaps, with structurally valid submissions, but 3/10 and 2/10 on boundary cases and 3/10 each on reciprocal cases, the same effect with the opposite value. Fifteen of their sixteen shared failures had identical failed field signatures, which the round read as a gap in protocol and competence rather than random noise.
against: The round says it "does not establish that candidate.5 is incorrect, that the broader typed representation is invalid, or that any pedagogical intervention is effective" (grade3-reading/bias_experiment/.agent/memory/G3_CANDIDATE5_ADDENDUM_ROUND_2026-07-16.md lines 116-118), and it qualified coders of a rule schema, not markers of student work.

evidence.quote: This is not a general schema or routing collapse. Missingness and scope-gap handling were perfect, positives and nearest neighbors were nearly perfect, and submissions were structurally valid. The discriminating failure is boundary/reciprocal reasoning, concentrated in typed force and value encoding:
Fifteen of the sixteen shared failures have identical failed field signatures.
The correlated error profile points to a protocol/competence boundary, not random reviewer noise.
